newsitem.title: USA: Sears earnings, uncollectible accounts both up.
newsitem.headline: Sears earnings, uncollectible accounts both up.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck & Co. said Thursday first-quarter earnings jumped more than 20 percent, thanks to solid gains in clothing and footwear sales.

The company said it earned $182 million, or 46 cents a share, in the first quarter, compared with year-earlier earnings of $151 million, or 36 cents a share. Revenues rose to $8.76 billion from $7.99 billion.

Despite the rise in earnings, the stock of the second-largest U.S. retailer fell in afternoon trading as investors focused on a sharp increase in Sears' domestic provision for uncollectible accounts, analysts said.
Sears' stock was off $1.375 at $47.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.

"The only item that looks like it should be causing some concern is the bad debt provision ... The market seems to be focusing on that issue," said Skip Helm, retail analyst at the William Blair & Co. brokerage and investment bank in Chicago.
Sears said its U.S. provision for uncollectible charge accounts rose 18.9 percent to $269 million in the first quarter from $227 million a year ago.

"The increase in account charge-offs reflects the continuation of an industry-wide increase in personal bankruptcies and delinquencies, as well as growth in the credit receivable portfolio," Sears said.

Other than the bad debt provision, analysts said Sears' first-quarter results looked good. The analysts' consensus earnings projection for the quarter had been 43 cents per share, according to First Call. Sears topped that by 3 cents.
"It's better than what the Street was looking for," Helm said.

Sears said strong first-quarter results were led by solid sales increases in apparel lines, including women's sportswear and dresses, children's apparel and footwear. Hardlines sales were led by lawn tractors and mowers as customers prepared for spring, the Hoffman Estates, Ill.-based retailer said.
"We continue to drive revenue increases through our off-the-mall growth strategy," said Chairman Arthur Martinez, referring to Sears' many smaller specialised stores.
He said Sears added more than 300 of the off-the-mall stores, which include hardware, furniture, automotive and dealer stores, since first quarter last year.
"Total off-the-mall store revenues grew nearly 17 percent in the quarter, including double-digit same-store sales increases in our hardware and dealer stores," Martinez said.
Sears said its gross profit margins as a percentage of its U.S. merchandise sales and services increased to 24.6 percent from 24.4 percent a year ago.
"Our gross margin rate continued to benefit from a shift in the balance of sales to higher-margin apparel merchandise," Martinez said.
The retailer also said it experienced a turnaround on the quarter in its 110 full-line, or traditional department store, Sears Canada unit.

Sears agreed two weeks ago to sell a controlling interest in its 42 store Sears Mexico unit. That sale contributed a $36 million loss to Sears international operations in the first quarter, it reported.
Sears operates 823 full-line stores and more than 2,500 off-the-mall stores.
